```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

shinyVIVO codes qualitative text against a set of themes with a large
language model running locally in [Ollama](https://ollama.com), then
compares a quantitative metric between texts with and without each theme.
You can do this point-and-click in the app, or from code.

## Set up Ollama

Install Ollama, then pull a model:

```
ollama pull llama3
```

Ollama listens on `http://localhost:11434`. Text is sent only to that
endpoint, so with the default setting it never leaves your machine.

## The app

```{r, eval = FALSE}
shinyVIVO::launch_app()
```

1. Upload a `.csv` or `.xlsx` file, or click **load the sample dataset**.
2. Pick the column holding the text and a numeric metric column.
3. Choose the model and type your themes, separated by commas.
4. Click **Run local AI coding**.

The **Coding matrix** tab shows one `TRUE`/`FALSE` column per theme, and
`NA` where the model call failed, so failures are never counted as "theme
absent". You can download it as a CSV. The **Mixed-methods plot** tab
compares the mean metric for rows with and without each theme.

## From code

The sample data has ten short feedback comments and a session-length metric:

```{r}
library(shinyVIVO)

feedback <- vivo_sample_data()
head(feedback, 3)
```

`code_dataframe()` codes every row with `ollama_code_text()`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
themes <- c("Frustration", "Bug Report", "Praise")
coded <- code_dataframe(feedback, text_col = "text", themes = themes,
                        model = "llama3")
```

To run this vignette without Ollama, pass a stand-in coder. Any function
that takes a text and the themes and returns a named logical vector works:

```{r}
keyword_coder <- function(text, themes, ...) {
  c(
    Frustration  = grepl("garbage|crazy|locked up|wiped", text),
    `Bug Report` = grepl("crash|bug|timeout|locked up", text),
    Praise       = grepl("fantastic|impressed|intuitive", text)
  )[themes]
}

themes <- c("Frustration", "Bug Report", "Praise")
coded <- code_dataframe(feedback, "text", themes, coder = keyword_coder)
coded[, c("user_id", themes)]
```

Then compare the metric by theme:

```{r}
summarise_theme_metric(coded, themes, "metric")
```

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Bar chart of mean session length with and without each theme."}
plot_theme_metric(coded, themes, "metric")
```

## Good practice

- **Validate first.** Have a person code a sample of the texts and check
  the model agrees before reporting results.
- **Treat results as associations.** A theme that goes with longer
  sessions does not cause them.
- **Pin the model.** Record the exact model name and version, since coding
  can change between model releases.
